Just for, you know, curiosity's sake, how would I go about doing that?

Slide a credit card (or other thin stiff material) in-between the door frame and the door knob, and pull the door open. You can unlock even main entrances to houses that way as long as there isn't a deadbolt.

If the knob has a hole in the center (most knobs for interior doors do), it is even easier. You will need a thin metal barrette. If the thinnest adult size will not fit in the hole, then locate one made for children. I have never had a problem getting the thinnest adult size to work though.

What you need to do is bend the barrette a bit so that it forms an L shape.

Then insert the flat end into the hole.

There is a groove (similar to the groove in the top of a screw) in the mechanism inside the knob. If you insert the barrette dead center and twist it a bit, you will feel it.
Once it is in the groove, turning the barrette like a key will pop the lock.
(Make sure you are turning in the opposite direction from which the lock turns to engage. )
